In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this is the first report of a 3-coordinate 16 VE Fe(III) complex with an eta 3-benzyl anion, and the first example of a 12 VE 3-coordinate Fe(II) complex with a (benzyl anion)-Fe(III) contact ion pair.
the 12 VE iron (II) benzyl [(nacnacs)-Fe(CH2-Ph)] is a 3-coordinate complex with a 3-electron 2-centre Fe-C bond.

the reaction of the benzyl anion with a 12 VE iron complex leads to the formation of a 14 VE iron(III) benzyl complex, which is then reduced back to the 12 VE iron benzyl complex by the benzyl anionic reagent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed the first 12VE iron(II) complex that is capable of abstracting a benzyl anion from a (beta diiminato) iron(II)benzyl complex.

the benzyl anion abstraction reaction is a very good probe for the electronic structure of the iron(II) complex and that the reaction is very sensitive to the electronic structure of [(nacnacs)Fe(CH2Ph)].

the (nacnac) ligand can be used to stabilise a 3-coordinate, 12 VE iron centre in a variety of oxidation states and the ligand is tolerant to both electrophilic and nucleophilic attack at the metal centre.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the 12 VE (nacnac)Fe(CH2Ph) is a competent nucleophile for the abstraction of the benzyl anion from B(C6F 5)(3), which is a very interesting result because the (nacnacs)Fe(III) complex is known to react with benzyl anion, and the (nacnaCs)Fe(II)/Fe(III) redox couple is known to be very facile.
